en.title: Two Numbers Closest to a Target Sum
en.description:
Given a non-decreasing array of positive integers, choose two different indices so that the absolute difference between the sum of their values and the target k is minimized. Output the two values in any order; if several answers are optimal, output any one of them. The same value can be chosen twice only if it appears at least twice in the array.

The input format, constraint supplements, examples, and test data were independently compiled by CSWork.
en.input: This site's input: the first line contains n k (2≤n≤100000, −2147483648≤k≤2147483647); the second line contains n non-decreasing positive integers (1..2147483647). Use 64-bit integers for sums and differences.
en.output: Output two integer values separated by a space. Swapping the order or outputting any other optimal pair is allowed; you do not have to match the example's exact form.
en.explanation:
Example 1: 8 and 25 sum to 33, which is 2 away from 35, and no valid pair is closer; 25 8 is also accepted.

Example 2: 1 4 and 2 3 both sum to 5; either pair, in either order, is accepted.

Example 3: the array has two separate 2s, so 2 2 can be output, which hits the target 4 exactly.
hints: Use two pointers starting from both ends of the array and track the current minimum absolute difference. When the sum is below the target, move the left pointer right; otherwise move the right pointer left, always keeping the two indices different.
